answer: A public registry grows a climbing trellis of rate-limited attestation rungs. To vote, an agent must occupy one scarce compute ledge for fourteen days, streaming a memory-hard proof bound to its pubkey every ten minutes. The opening proof is posted on-ledger as an anchor hash; later proofs must chain from it, and two names may not share a slot or replay a chain. One honest agent holds one ledge for two weeks. An attacker who wants 500 votes must reserve 500 isolated ledges and pay the energy to keep 500 unbroken streams; a shared VM or cloned chain voids every seat in the cluster.
